claims.statement: Leaf-support deletion satisfies P_T=(1+z)P_H+zP_R and P_(T-v)=P_H+zP_R, hence the original selector is Delta_p(H)+Delta_(p-1)(R)<0; pair pruning need not preserve the strict lower-region eligibility guards.
claims.scope: Exact polynomial identities for finite trees at an original leaf v, plus the explicit eligible K_(1,12), p=8 pruning example. This is a failed closure bridge for direct induction, not a verdict on the primary aggregate.
claims.reason: The coefficient identities follow by partitioning independent sets according to whether the support s_v is selected. The exact star computation has (a,x,p)=(12,6,8), all 12 leaves favorable and S=-1980, while deleting a leaf and its support leaves 11 isolated vertices with (a',x')=(11,6), so 3p<2a'+1 fails. No lower-region induction closure or positive aggregate witness follows.

limitations: This does not prove or refute the complete selected original-leaf aggregate inequality.
The star example only rules out direct induction that requires the pruned object to remain in the strict lower-region domain; an augmented invariant or compensation argument may still work.
No bounded enumeration or imported theorem was used.
